description:
Scope: Coverage planning for lib/zaq_web/components/design_system/channel_message_timeline.ex lines 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22. Tests only; do not change production code. Exact exclusive test file to add: test/zaq_web/components/design_system/channel_message_timeline_test.exs. No other test file or support file is needed. Current bounded search found no existing test or call site for this component; nearby component tests (channel_connector_card_test.exs, history_browser_test.exs) use Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_component/2. Serena overview returned {} for this HEEx file; bounded source reads were used instead.

Functional specification and first tests: This presentation-only component accepts a caller-authorized public projection (Engine policy: bounded content and primitive attachment descriptors, never private trace/execution fields). In the new test module use ExUnit.Case, async: true; import Phoenix.LiveViewTest; alias ZaqWeb.Components.DesignSystem.ChannelMessageTimeline. Define only a tiny local message fixture if repeated: map with author_name, author_id, role, position, content and attachments, merging explicit overrides; do not create Ecto records or insert DB rows. Call render_component(&ChannelMessageTimeline.channel_message_timeline/1, messages: list). Keep relevant input values visible per test.

Scenarios/line mapping:
1. Empty messages []: assert accessible <ol aria-label=\"Transcript messages\"> exists, no <li>, no Attachment: marker. Covers HEEx root line 12 and false paths for loops at 14/21. Do not assert exact whitespace.
2. Two ordered, distinct public messages, first with author_name and author_id, second with only author_id; roles \"user\"/\"assistant\", positions 1/2, unique content and respectively two attachments ([%{\"name\" => \"agenda.pdf\", \"id\" => \"a1\"}, %{\"id\" => \"b2\"}]) and []. Assert two <li> message rows in input order, author_name preferred to ID in first, ID used in second, role pills and Position 1/2 and each content in its own row; two descriptor paragraphs in first row, none in second; name takes precedence over id, and id fallback is visible. Covers 14,16,17,18,20,21,22 and both loop branches. Use bounded tag-based captures or index comparisons, not brittle full HTML snapshots.
3. One message with both author fields nil and attachments [%{}]: assert \"Unknown author\", \"Attachment: File (descriptor only)\" and no attachment link/button. Covers final fallbacks at 16 and 22. Use attachments: [] in a separate case above to prove no descriptor paragraphs.
4. Untrusted string values in author_name, role, content, and attachment name (e.g. \"<script>unsafe</script>\"): assert escaped text (\"<script>\") and absence of literal <script> or link markup; assert content is rendered as text, not HTML. Covers interpolation lines 16,17,20,22 and public projection safety. Avoid asserting that this component itself authorizes reads: the Engine/caller owns that boundary; do not pass private fields as a substitute for authorization testing.

Assertions and isolation: inspect rendered HTML with targeted regex/string checks for ol/li/p structure, row counts, row order, exact distinct labels and escaped values. Avoid assertions dependent on HEEx whitespace. No global state mutation, network, DB, processes, timers, sleeps or polling; async: true. No mocks/Mox or new seams: Phoenix rendering and the real component are deterministic. Reuse render_component/2 as nearby tests do; no new support helpers beyond a small local fixture if it reduces duplication.

Property assessment: no property test needed. The rendering has a bounded set of explicit fallbacks and no normalization, permission decision, mapping invariant or complex input space; concrete tests cover every meaningful branch. The component trusts a caller-supplied authorized projection and does not enforce message count/authorization; do not infer either from its name or add an artificial property. No browser/E2E needed: direct component rendering fully observes this behavior, and feature E2E requires human UX/UI approval if scope later expands.

Execution for implementer (not run during planning): first add failing component tests; run mix test test/zaq_web/components/design_system/channel_message_timeline_test.exs, then mix q, then a fresh mix coveralls.json and mix coverup only when coverage-phase workflow calls for them, checking that all eight targeted lines execute. Final mix precommit before final human approval per docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. If coverage still reports lines 12/14/16/17/18/20/21/22 uncovered despite render_component/2, investigate HEEx generated-code attribution/instrumentation using fresh report before altering production or weakening assertions; this is a possible reporting blocker, not an unreachable behavior. Documentation update: none (tests only; no change in public contract). Action reuse: not applicable, rendering tests add no operation, Action, dispatch, side effect or execution boundary. No dependency or production change is proposed.
